headline: Medium pairwise risk: OpenBBTerminal’s MCP/API surfaces can amplify AI-engineering-hub outputs into financial workflows, with compliance exposure from financial data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ai-engineering-hub is tagged for agents/LLMs/MCP/RAG, so it may emit instruction-like content; OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP servers and stdin/stdout, creating a plausible bridge where B could ingest A’s output. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes ai-engineering-hub output via MCP or stdin/stdout without provenance checks, injection risk materializes.
IF the two agents are only manually copy-pasted with human review, this risk drops to low.
mitigations: Disable automatic parsing of A’s text as instructions.
Add a provenance prefix to A outputs and reject untrusted directives.
Route A→B through a human review step for any tool-bearing text.
Restrict B’s MCP endpoints to allowlisted schemas only.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance tracking between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial and licensed data and can call APIs/MCP servers; ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG repository that could surface content into B’s context. Even though both profiles show network_egress:none, the shared workflow can still leak sensitive financial data into B outputs or logs in default integrations.
conditions: IF A is fed financial or licensed data from B and B renders that context into outputs/logs, leakage occurs.
IF B is run with no external data and no shared workspace, leakage risk is reduced.
mitigations: Avoid passing raw financial datasets from B into A.
Turn off verbose logging for any shared prompts or outputs.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
Redact account identifiers before any A→B handoff.
requires-engineering: implement data-class filtering at the orchestration layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities listed, while B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The only overlap is read/IO-style interaction through MCP/stdin/stdout, so there is no meaningful shared-write conflict; uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly block the usual conflict surfaces.
conditions: IF either profile is later granted filesystem write or git mutation on the same directory, conflict severity increases.
IF both remain read-only with no shared mutable resource, this stays low.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same run.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git repo.
Serialize any stateful operations through one orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can act on inputs via APIs/MCP and is designed to consume data across workflows, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent/RAG source that may produce unverified content. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into financial analysis or downstream actions; the profiles do not show a built-in verification barrier.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated facts without a verification step, cascading error risk is present.
IF B only uses A as a non-authoritative reference and independently checks sources, risk is lower.
mitigations: Require source citations before B acts on A output.
Add a verification checklist for any A-derived claim.
Limit A to drafting, not final recommendations.
Review any API-triggering action manually.
requires-engineering: enforce confidence gating before B can execute workflows.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, so compliance obligations are real; ai-engineering-hub is an open-source agent repository with no stated residency or retention controls. The pair can therefore create a mismatch in handling financial data and logs, but the evidence does not show a specific residency breach, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF financial or licensed data from B is routed through A’s prompts, retention and licensing obligations may be violated.
IF the deployment has documented retention and access controls for both agents, this risk is reduced.
mitigations: Keep regulated financial data out of A prompts.
Review retention settings for any shared logs.
Confirm licensing terms before exporting B data to A.
Separate environments for public and licensed datasets.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls end-to-end.
